exercise.name: Smith Single Leg Deadlift

reference.title: Smith Single Leg Deadlift
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page could not be fetched from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.bodyPart: Hips (glutes) and back of the thighs

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace while balancing at the top, hold it on the way down and back up, breathe out at the top.
breathing.cadence: About 2.2 s down, a short pause, about 1.4 s up

prescription.tempo: Slow and balanced: 2 s down, short pause, 1-1.5 s up
prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen and well below a two-leg deadlift: balance and a flat back come first (about 3 reps in reserve).
prescription.progression: Add 2.5 kg once every rep stays balanced with the hips square.

cues.text: Stand on the right leg under the Smith bar, knee soft, bar in front of the thighs with an overhand grip just outside the hips; turn it off the pegs and lift the left foot just off the floor.
Hinge at the right hip: the chest goes down as the left leg reaches straight back and the bar runs down the rails in front of the standing leg; hips stay square to the floor.
Stop with the trunk and the back leg close to one line, near level, back flat.
Drive the right hip forward to stand tall, the back leg swinging down under you.
Find your balance before the next rep; do all reps, then switch legs.

mistakes.mistake: Hips opening up (the back-leg hip turning toward the ceiling)
mistakes.fix: Point the back toes at the floor and keep both hip bones level.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the back to reach down
mistakes.fix: Go only as low as a flat back allows.
Keep a soft, fixed knee; the hips move back.
Slow down, look at the floor a metre or two ahead, use a lighter bar.

kinematics.norm: Hinge until the trunk is near level, flat back (clinical opinion); unilateral barbell work loads the standing-side hip extensors (Mausehund 2019)
Standing knee soft, about 15-25 degrees (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Hovering beside the standing ankle (toe 9.1 cm up)
kinematics.peak: Hip-to-ankle line 177.4° to the trunk line (180 = one straight line), pelvis level
kinematics.norm: Back leg in line with the trunk, toes down, pelvis level (common coaching)

kinematics.setup: Overhand, 50 cm grip (handle centres), bar against the thighs
kinematics.peak: 41.7 cm at the bottom (38 cm along the rails); hands' midpoint within 0.04 cm of the rail line at every key
kinematics.norm: Bar hangs under the shoulders, close to the standing leg; fixed by the guide rails: the bar can only travel along them (here a rail line fitted to the free-bar path, a few degrees from vertical at most)

kinematics.peak: 2.2 s down, 0.4 s pause, 1.4 s up, 1.4 s reset
kinematics.norm: Slow and controlled for balance (clinical opinion)

cautions: Set the safety stops just under the lowest bar position before the first rep; the bar cannot go lower than them.
Practise turning the bar on and off the pegs (a small turn of the wrists) with an empty bar first.
The rails fix the bar path: place yourself so the movement feels natural for the joints, and do not force range.
The rails take care of the bar's balance, not yours: learn the single-leg hinge with body weight first.
Low-back pain: shorten the range or use a kickstand stance.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Balance: lightly touch the back toes down (kickstand) or hold a wall with one hand and a dumbbell in the other.
progressions: Slower lowering with a pause at the bottom.

muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Standing-leg hip extensor, lengthened in the hinge (Lee 2018 for the Romanian style).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Drives the standing hip forward to stand tall and keeps the pelvis level (Mausehund 2019).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis level over one leg.
muscleNotes.core: Resists rotation of the pelvis over one leg (Saeterbakken 2012 for unilateral work).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Hold the shoulders against the bar.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Hold the shoulders against the bar.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Lifts the back leg in line with the trunk.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Help lift and hold the back leg.
